effect: Can greatly lower levels of HIV medicines (e.g. protease inhibitors, nevirapine), risking treatment failure and resistance.

effect: Higher risk of sunburn-like skin reactions with photosensitising antibiotics (tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones).
mechanism: Additive photosensitivity: psoralens are phototoxic, and these antibiotics are common photosensitisers.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Avoid sun exposure.

effect: May add to sun sensitivity (burning, rash) caused by photosensitising medicines such as tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, thiazides, isotretinoin or amiodarone.
mechanism: Hypericin in St John's wort causes photosensitivity; the EU monograph advises avoiding intense UV exposure and NCCIH notes severe skin reactions after sun exposure. Additive effect with photosensitising drugs is inferred.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Use sun protection and avoid intense UV exposure.

effect: Can lower levels of cancer medicines such as irinotecan, imatinib and docetaxel, making them less effective.
mechanism: St John's wort induces CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and P-glycoprotein, lowering blood levels of many medicines; the effect rises with hyperforin content and lasts about a week after stopping. Irinotecan active-metabolite levels fell by about 42% and imatinib exposure fell in clinical studies; contraindicated with cytostatics metabolised by these pathways.
advice: Avoid this combination. Tell your oncology team about all supplements.

effect: Ginger was linked to raised crizotinib levels and liver injury in a cancer patient.
mechanism: Probable CYP3A4 inhibition; single case report.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your cancer team about ginger supplements.

effect: Reported liver injury when combined with imatinib.
mechanism: Case report of imatinib hepatotoxicity after 3 months of Panax ginseng energy drinks, possibly via CYP3A4 effects. LiverTox notes ginseng may cause herb-drug interactions leading to liver injury.
advice: Tell your oncology team before using ginseng. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Green tea polyphenols may block the effect of bortezomib and related boronic-acid cancer medicines.
mechanism: EGCG binds the boronic acid group and prevented bortezomib-induced tumour cell death in cell and mouse studies (preclinical, but on-target).
advice: Tell your oncology team before using green tea extracts during cancer treatment. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Curcumin lowered blood levels of tamoxifen and its active form endoxifen, which might reduce its effect.
mechanism: Clinical PK study in breast-cancer patients: endoxifen AUC fell 7.7% with curcumin and 12.4% with curcumin + piperine.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your cancer team about any curcumin supplement.

effect: Possible interaction with letrozole was predicted, but a clinical study found none.
mechanism: Cinnamaldehyde inactivates CYP2A6 in vitro (NCCIH notes theoretical concern); a 2026 clinical study of Ceylon cinnamon found no change in letrozole or nicotine levels.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May change docetaxel clearance in some people.

effect: May add to the risk of liver injury with medicines that can affect the liver.
mechanism: Giloy linked to autoimmune-like liver injury in case series; additive risk theoretical.

effect: May add to liver injury risk with other liver-affecting medicines.

effect: May slightly add to bleeding tendency alongside newer oral blood thinners.

effect: Can greatly lower levels of HIV medicines (e.g. protease inhibitors, nevirapine), risking treatment failure and resistance.

effect: Can sharply lower blood levels of some HIV medicines (saquinavir), risking treatment failure and resistance.

advice: Avoid garlic supplements with HIV protease inhibitors unless your HIV doctor agrees. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Do not change HIV medicine routines without your HIV clinician.

effect: Unlikely to change nevirapine levels at food-like doses.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Avoid taking them at the same time and monitor your blood pressure.

mechanism: St John's wort induces CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and P-glycoprotein, lowering blood levels of many medicines; the effect rises with hyperforin content and lasts about a week after stopping. advice: Tell your oncology team before using ginseng. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

mechanism: EGCG binds the boronic acid group and prevented bortezomib-induced tumour cell death in cell and mouse studies (preclinical, but on-target).
advice: Tell your oncology team before using green tea extracts during cancer treatment. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your cancer team about any curcumin supplement.

effect: Can lower levels of cancer medicines such as irinotecan, imatinib and docetaxel, making them less effective.

effect: Reported liver injury when combined with imatinib.

advice: Tell your oncology team before using green tea extracts during cancer treatment. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Curcumin lowered blood levels of tamoxifen and its active form endoxifen, which might reduce its effect.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your cancer team about any curcumin supplement.

effect: Possible interaction with letrozole was predicted, but a clinical study found none.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May change docetaxel clearance in some people.

effect: Can lower levels of cancer medicines such as irinotecan, imatinib and docetaxel, making them less effective.
mechanism: St John's wort induces CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and P-glycoprotein, lowering blood levels of many medicines; the effect rises with hyperforin content and lasts about a week after stopping. advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Ginger was linked to raised crizotinib levels and liver injury in a cancer patient.
mechanism: Probable CYP3A4 inhibition; single case report.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your cancer team about ginger supplements.

effect: Reported liver injury when combined with imatinib.
mechanism: Case report of imatinib hepatotoxicity after 3 months of Panax ginseng energy drinks, possibly via CYP3A4 effects. LiverTox notes ginseng may cause herb-drug interactions leading to liver injury.
advice: Tell your oncology team before using ginseng. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Green tea polyphenols may block the effect of bortezomib and related boronic-acid cancer medicines.
mechanism: EGCG binds the boronic acid group and prevented bortezomib-induced tumour cell death in cell and mouse studies (preclinical, but on-target).
advice: Tell your oncology team before using green tea extracts during cancer treatment. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Raises cyclosporine blood levels, risking toxicity.
mechanism: In kidney-transplant recipients, berberine 0.2 g three times daily raised cyclosporine trough levels and AUC (about 35% higher AUC); attributed to CYP3A4 and intestinal P-gp inhibition.
advice: Avoid unless your transplant team approves and monitors levels. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May raise tacrolimus blood levels (kidney harm reported in one case), although another monitored patient showed no change.
mechanism: Probable CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition by curcumin; raised tacrolimus levels in rats and one case report; a second case found no effect at culinary doses.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. If you take tacrolimus or cyclosporine, levels may need extra monitoring.

effect: Could in theory work against immune-suppressing medicines.
mechanism: Immunostimulant activity of andrographolide and extracts in experimental studies; no human interaction data.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Possible interaction with letrozole was predicted, but a clinical study found none.
mechanism: Cinnamaldehyde inactivates CYP2A6 in vitro (NCCIH notes theoretical concern); a 2026 clinical study of Ceylon cinnamon found no change in letrozole or nicotine levels.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May change docetaxel clearance in some people.
mechanism: Clinical PK study found no significant change overall, but possible reduced clearance in CYP3A5*1A carriers.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: theoretical reduction in the effect of immune-suppressing medicines
mechanism: product studied as an immunomodulatory herbo-mineral formulation (animal data); interaction theoretical
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Phyto-oestrogens could theoretically interfere with hormone-based cancer medicines (e.g. tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors).
mechanism: Isoflavone phyto-oestrogen content; no interaction studies.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Tell your oncology team about all supplements.

effect: Could in theory work against immune-suppressing medicines.
mechanism: Picroliv (iridoid glycoside fraction) stimulated antibody and cell-mediated immune responses in mice; no human interaction data.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining. Especially relevant after an organ transplant.

effect: May work against medicines that dampen the immune system.
mechanism: Immune-stimulating activity of neem preparations in animals; theoretical.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May add to the immune-suppressing effect of these medicines.

effect: Can lower rivaroxaban/apixaban levels and reduce protection against clots.
mechanism: St John's wort induces CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and P-glycoprotein, lowering blood levels of many medicines; the effect rises with hyperforin content and lasts about a week after stopping. The rivaroxaban label says to avoid combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers such as St John's wort.
advice: Avoid this combination. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May raise levels of CYP3A4-metabolised medicines.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May raise blood levels of medicines broken down by CYP3A4.
mechanism: Bark extracts strongly inhibited CYP3A4 in human liver microsomes (IC50 < 50 µg/mL); not tested in people.
advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: may raise levels of medicines broken down by CYP3A4

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May raise blood levels of medicines broken down by CYP3A4.

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: May raise blood levels of medicines broken down by CYP3A4.

effect: may raise levels of medicines broken down by CYP3A4

advice: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining.

effect: Could raise blood levels of narrow-margin medicines cleared by CYP3A4 (e.g. tacrolimus, cyclosporine).

advice: Tell your surgeon, anaesthetist and dentist that you take it. It is commonly advised to stop the herb about 2 weeks before planned surgery; ask your doctor.

effect: May cause blood-pressure and heart-rhythm instability during anaesthesia.

advice: Tell your surgeon or anaesthetist; they may advise pausing Bala products before a planned procedure.

effect: May increase bleeding during and after surgery.
